cohort: The study included 50 women who had undergone cesarean sections with spinal anesthesia at Al-Mubarak Hospital Sadiqabad, with a mean age of 29.29 +/- 2.44 years and a mean BMI of 24.38 +/- 1.72.
finding: The study found significant associations between post-cesarean back pain and both maternal and surgical factors, particularly highlighting the importance of procedural considerations like the number of lumbar puncture attempts and needle size.
mod_finding: The study focused on post-cesarean back pain in women who underwent spinal anesthesia for their cesarean sections, implying the mode of birth (C-section) as a prerequisite for the studied outcome.
gest_age: Cesarean sections were performed at 38.04 +/- 0.80 weeks of gestation.
